task: Yes. We just need a pilot to steal the stealth ship prototype from the secret peleng base located on <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. Three of our commandos will accompany you. We don't expect that you'll even have to touch a weapon, <Ranger>. However, you must understand all the dangers of this venture. Ideally, you'll be taken straight to the hangar, and at that point everything will depend purely on your piloting skills. We trust you can arrive at the destination by <Date>, yes?
success:
You’ve exceeded all our expectations, <Ranger>! You managed to survive, despite the despicable efforts of those peleng cutthroats to eliminate our landing team, and deliver the stealth ship unharmed. For this we are happy to give you <Money> credits. We would have liked to add a bonus for your great skill, but we need to send that money to the families of the deceased commandos. We're confident you won’t be opposed.
The funny thing is that the pelengs haven't used any outdoor surveillance to protect the stealth ship... No special lenses or monitors, for example. If you have a ship like that, you think you'd want to have at least a few safeguards. Do you agree? Well, anyway, I won't keep you any longer. I know your time is valuable, ranger.

loc.51.0:
A couple of hours later you found yourself bouncing in the backseat of an armored vehicle. You were somewhat alarmed by the fact that there were only two commandos escorting you instead of the promised three. In any event, watching this duo, who are armed from head to toe, was pretty interesting. A wiry faeyan with a sniper rifle on his back was driving and bickering with an unusually-crimson maloq.
"That's what I'm telling you. What's the point of giving yourself away by shooting from that medieval piece of crap?" he said, pointing at the maloq's shotgun. "It's better to lie low and pick them off one by one like chickens with my plasma gun - no noise, no smoke."
"Hey, you facet-eyed loser. I told you, it's 'No noise, no mess.' Get it right!" growled the maloq with furrowed brows. "You can't even hold a hovergun in your hands - and you're try to tell me?! Remember, strength and firepower DECIDE THE BATTLE!" grunted the red giant as he looked fondly at the six-barreled gun mounted in the firing hole.
"What about range? And accuracy? Huh?! Naw, I have no need for these noisemakers!" retorted the faeyan.
"Heh, heh. Who's offering? I certainly won’t give you a gun. If you knew something about them, things would be different."
"I'd share my weapons with a competent humanoid, but certainly not with you..." There was a clatter.
The bushy trees of planet <ToPlanet> were sweeping by outside the window. The car was jumping along the twisted path toward the secret peleng base. Your escorts were hardly paying any attention to you, and you wanted to:
loc.51.1:
The commandos started to squabble again.
"You say 'accuracy'. But you're only accurate when you're sneaking. How about when you're walking or running? When you can’t take good aim of the target, that’s when a shotgun is pretty useful. Kaboom! ...it has a big effect on just about everyone."
"Uh-huh. Sure. Like the last time, when your drumrolling attracted even more of them. Shoot silent and sure!" said the driver, seemingly pleased about the saying he had just come up with. Smiling, he sat back cozily in his seat.
"Ha! That's what grenades are for! Throw one into a pack of six-paws and then shoot like mad all around the bush. Then you won't have so many attackers. And if any of them come to, throw another grenade over. Easy peasy!" said the maloq. Then he started moving his lips and frowning. It looked like he was working through the situation again in his head. Then, looking pleased with the outcome of his imaginary attack, he leaned back on the seat.
loc.52.0:
A few loud pops stopped the car on the path - bullets had ripped through the front tires. The armored offroad vehicle started to pitch to the side as you heard the ear-splitting sounds of bullets hitting the car body. The faeyan yanked the steering wheel hard and said,
"Damn! I didn't expect the mercs so soon!!!" The car jerked to one side and hit a bump. You injured your head on the ceiling.
The last thing you saw was the maloq grasping for his machine gun and shooting through the side firing hole and screaming,
"I'll get you, you animals! Arrrrggghhh!"
You fainted for a moment. When you opened your eyes, the acrid smoke began to sting them. Through clouds of dense smoke you could see that the car had embedded its nose in a ditch on the side of the road. Its front-end was in flames and your military escorts were motionless. Blood flowed from their armed bodies. The car could explode at any moment, so you've got to do something.
loc.53.0:
You push the box out of the trunk and jumped out behind it. You crouched down, so your enemies wouldn't spot you... Then there was an explosion! Fragments of metal flew all around. Some splintered branches fell to the ground. Just like your initial plan to capture the stealth ship prototype. Now you must face the cutthroats who are scattered across the forest alone. You don't want to show any signs of your escape. Before you throw the box into the bushes you try to assess what it holds - it may be useful.
<clr>The boxes full of accessories that you can attach to your belt keep your hands free. However, usually only one of them can be attached to your belt at a time.<clrEnd>
loc.55.0:
You clear your throat and blurted out,
"Only energy firecrackers are just for sissies! They're only good for burning cockroaches! An old-fashioned firearm, that's what a real man uses. But what would a hermaphrodite know about it?
"Ha, ha, ha, Ha!" laughs the red-faced maloq loudly. "Right on, man! Her math for diet! Exactly!" He slapped the driver on the shoulder.
"Multi-gendered morons," hissed the faeyan. He jabbed the maloq's shoulder and clenched the steering wheel more firmly. "You two numskulls certainly couldn't hit a silver credit at 200 yards."
loc.57.0:
"The art of being a true warrior is staying invisible for the enemy and methodically cutting down its forces with an elegant energy weapon..." Two bickering commandos turned and looked at you attentively. You carried on. "Of course, if you don't have any brains you can use your head to deflect projectiles," you said, winking at the faeyan.
The maloq’s face turned three different colors at the same time. He jumped up.
"Are you getting sassy with me or what?"
"Calm down. Of course, not," said the faeyan helpfully. "Surely, he meant the planetary fighting with the dominators. Some of their battle machines have empty titanium casing instead of proper units equipped with electronics. They use them to deflect projectiles," said the driver, not suppressing his laughter very well. But the maloq seemed to have calmed down.
"What planetary fighting? Are you screwing with me? Bah, go hang yourselves, smartasses," the maloq said and turned back to the window. And with a businesslike air, he adjusted the machine gun.
loc.59.0: It took nearly a day to get back. You were bleeding from the scratches you received from the thorns in the bushes on planet <ToPlanet>. Starving and infuriated with this blasted mission, you at last dive into your home ship. You'd rather be alive without any honor than be dead.
loc.61.0: You crouched down in the bushes not far from the remains of your armored car.
loc.61.1:
Your mission remains the same: you must steal the stealth ship from the hangar east of here. Your military escorts are dead, so you'll have to make your way there on your own. The important thing is to stay alert and remain calm. There may be pelengs nearby straining their ears toward the forest. Loud firearms will get their attention at a distance, but energy weapons will give you away at close range. Anyone nearby will be able to find you easily.
And once spotted, you probably won't be able to hide again. Once you're a target, it's better to run and shoot. Although you can't shoot as accurately while running, it also becomes harder for the enemy to hit you.
There's more bad news: reinforcements have been sent to the site of the explosion to comb over the area. Oh well, more enemies means more fun!

loc.100.0:
"We're getting close now," said the faeyan after checking the radar on the instrument panel. The rest of the path is guarded, so we will park the car in these bushes. Then we'll have to shoot our way through, but there shouldn't be too many guards.
"Ha! No problem! Five, and maybe the personnel at the hangar," said the maloq, smoothing his eyebrows and affectionately checking the machine gun mounted in the firing hole. "Bang, bang, bang!" he laughed, pretending to shoot at the trees that swept past outside the window.
"Anyway, if we are spotted..." said the driver, looking sideways at the maloq, "they can send a hoverjet with <clr>reinforcements from the neighboring base<clrEnd>. <clr>It's an hour by flight.<clrEnd>"
"Is the stealth ship ready for flying?" you ask.
"How would we know?" interjected the maloq. "That's your job: filling it with fuel… You know, washing the windows, cleaning the ashtray! Ha, ha, ha, Ha!"

loc.137.0: The support fell off, and the gate started leaning outward. Soon it crashed to the ground, raising clouds of dust... As the dust settled, you could see a peleng with a plasma gun pointed at you. He is much closer to you than you are to the hatch of the ship. Trying to escape would be a really bad idea.
loc.138.0:
You put your hands in the air... But, unexpectedly, the peleng puts his gun down and raises one of his four arms.
"And hello to you too,<Ranger>! Sorry I was late getting to the armored car. I slept in. You know how that goes," he said with a guilty smile.
"You bastard! Your partners are dead and I’ve done your entire job, all because you 'overslept'."
"Come on, calm down. I have a deal for you: I'll buy the <clr>mercenaries' dogtags from you for 50 cr. a piece<clrEnd>," he said, pointing his finger at chains dangling out of your pocket, "and do you pretend in front of my bosses that everything went according to plan. Deal?"
loc.139.0:
You charged that the peleng desperately, swinging your fists, but he dodged your attack.
"Hey, <Ranger>! What are you doing hitting an ally?!! Yeah, I was late for the armored car. So what?" He put his plasma gun side and his face twisted into a guilty smile.
"You bastard! Your partners are dead and I’ve done your entire job - and you're pointing a gun at me!"
"Come on, calm down. I have a deal for you: I'll buy the <clr>mercenaries' dogtags <clrEnd> from you for 50 cr. a piece," he said, pointing his finger at chains dangling out of your pocket, "and do you pretend in front of my bosses that everything went according to plan. Deal?"
loc.142.0:
"So... I owe you {[p11]*50} in cash for the dogtags." The peleng pulled out his credit card ran his fingers over the buttons on it, and pointed it at your credit card. The transaction completed successfully and, in a noticeably more relaxed atmosphere, you both got into the stealth ship.
In an hour, with the invisibility feature turned off, you were back at the agreed location. Your client's representatives thanked you for your great work.
They quickly loaded in and disappeared into the distance. You stared after them with a smile on your face. One of planet <ToPlanet>'s gorgeous sunsets was reflecting in the "Megavision" glasses
loc.143.0:
The peleng hopped in after you and sat down quietly in the back seat. You gave him a passing glance and then skillfully piloted the ship out of the hangar. You rapidly accelerated to Mach two. In an hour, you are at the prearranged location, with the ship's camouflage disabled.
Your client's representatives thanked you for your great work and took the peleng into custody for desertion. However, they refused to pay any extra for your valor, citing the serious physical damage to the charred armored car.
"Our brave commandos wouldn’t have been ambushed that easily if you hadn’t distracted them with your mmm... spontaneous behavior."
They quickly loaded in and disappeared into the distance. You stared after them with a smile on your face. One of planet <ToPlanet>'s gorgeous sunsets was reflecting in the "Megavision" glasses
loc.144.0:
A traitorous misfire thundered across the hangar.
"Heh, heh. Hey, my clip is full," said the peleng with an evil grin. "Just don't chicken out, <Ranger>. I am your friend! Sorry I was late getting to the armored car. I slept in. You know how that goes."
"You bastard! Your partners are dead and I’ve done your entire job, all because you 'overslept'."
"Come on, calm down. I have a deal for you: I'll buy the <clr>mercenaries' dogtags <clrEnd> from you for 50 cr. a piece," he said, pointing his finger at chains dangling out of your pocket, "and do you pretend in front of my bosses that everything went according to plan. Deal?"
loc.146.0:
The rattle of a hoverjet shattered the tranquility of the forest, and you could see the fast combat aircraft flying over the path, leaving a trail of parachuting <clr>mercenaries from the group of reinforcements<clrEnd>.
You try to stay out of sight while the aircraft flies away.

loc.148.0:
You climb deftly up the ladder into the ship and immediately secured the hatch. Without any delay, you fired at the back wall of the hangar and quickly flew out. Swinging all four of his arms, the peleng chased after you for a long time.
In an hour, with the invisibility feature turned off, you were back at the agreed location. Your client's representatives thanked you for your great work. However, they expressed regret that their three commandos didn't returned from the mission. You clarified how many military escorts had actually shown up. It turns out that the third one was supposed to be a peleng with a plasma gun. You didn’t add anything further; you just politely bid them farewell.
They quickly loaded in and disappeared into the distance. You stared after them with a smile on your face. One of planet <ToPlanet>'s gorgeous sunsets was reflecting in the "Megavision" glasses

jump.59.desc:
You stretched yourself out onto the backseat and quickly slipped into slumber; the stress of recent days was apparent. You had a dream. In your dream, you lay on some grass in an unfamiliar forest. All of a sudden, the sky was filled with storm clouds, and huge monsters appeared from behind the trees. They wandered around, making the earth shake with their heavy steps, but they still didn’t notice you. Suddenly, all the monsters turned towards you, stretched out their paws to you, and started to surround you. They look very menacing. One of them bent down and looked straight into your eyes. Then he pulled out a pistol and shot...
You woke up in terror and saw your military escorts in the front seats, listening with pricked ears.
jump.60.text: Ask the maloq to give you a weapon
jump.60.desc:
"Come on, relax! We'll deliver you straight to the hangar gate. And we'll shoot all the six-paws that turn up along the way. We're almost there.
"But you're armed to the teeth, can I at least have something too?" you cry out.
"Fine. Here's a knife - take it. Good for fighting butterflies. Ha, ha, ha, Ha!" The crimson-faced commando threw you a decent-sized <clr>maloq machete<clrEnd> in a leather scabbard. "Give it back to me when the job's done. I'll need it to chop up the pelengs for the soup," he said and started to laugh again.
"You mean butterflies? I don’t think the mercenaries will just stick out their necks for me, and it’s not beans their guns are loaded with!"
"Well, if you fight as well as you can yap, you'll be able to sneak up from behind and use the blade. But I wouldn't suggest attacking a crowd - they'll fill you with lead or something else! Anyway, don’t lose your medical kit," said the giant, nodding toward the box on the floor.
jump.62.text: Support the maloq in the argument
jump.63.text: Ask the maloq to give you a weapon
jump.63.desc:
"Hey, pal. Would you lend me a gun? I just want to make a few holes in these froggers."
"A comedian like you deserves a proper shotgun," said the maloq. He threw you a heavy gun. It smacked your hands hard, but you stopped yourself from wincing. You grabbed the <clr>shotgun<clrEnd> and worked the action - everything is in order. You can shoot pelengs from the hip with that, even when you're running. If it doesn't kill them, it'll wound them at the very least.
All of the sudden, your escort woke up, and the armored car slowed down.
jump.64.text: Support the faeyan in the argument
jump.65.text: Ask the faeyan to give you a weapon
jump.65.desc:
"Hey, sir. Would you let me borrow your sniper rifle during the operation?"
"No."
"Why not?"
"What a caveman!" said the driver, turning to the maloq. "How do I explain the basics of private property to our guest? It must be total anarchy on there on planet <FromPlanet>: 'take whatever isn't chained to the floor'," he said. Then replied angrily, "The rifle is mine, that's why."
"I'll pay to rent it then!"
"What a pest! Fine, take this. The battery is almost dead anyway," said the faeyan. He pulled out the handle of a <clr>laser sword<clrEnd> and handed it to you. "This will help in an emergency. Just don't get burned - we'll fail the mission if we don't have a pilot. You'd better take a medical kit just in case."
You carefully took the weighty handle. It had an activation button and a worn inscription on the metal: "Nuke Skyliner". This is no Jedi fairy tale, but it may come in handy in face-to-face combat with an armed mercenary.
jump.66.text: Ask the faeyan to give you a weapon
jump.66.desc:
"My hermaphrodite friend, can I demonstrate my great skill with weapons to you?"
"I don't see why not. This ought to do..." said the faeyan, extracting a plasma musket from a long holster on his belt." This weapon distinguishes true warriors from savages.
You were pleased to take the <clr>streamlined plasma musket<clrEnd>. Accurate, quiet, and simple to operate! Not very powerful, but who cares! But the maloq interrupted your thoughts. He grabbed his machine gun and peered out into the forest, as if looking for something. The faeyan slowed down and started listening intently.
jump.67.text: Ask the faeyan to give you a weapon
jump.67.desc:
In reply to your question, the driver only sniffed in contempt. Then he leaned slightly forward to the lookout window:
"What the...?!"
jump.68.text: Ask the maloq to give you a weapon
jump.68.desc: "Keep quiet, so I don't smash your head in!" snarled the maloq. He turned back to the lookout window. His eyes caught sight of an object as it flew by. He suddenly grabbed his machine gun. "Dammit!"
jump.69.desc:
The enormous, crimson-faced maloq went limp. But he still had a death grip on the machine gun with his big hands. That made it much more difficult to drag the body. You had only made it about thirty feet from the car when a huge explosion tore the vehicle to pieces. The blast sent you reeling. A few pieces of metal whizzed right over your head. You got down and examined the maloq, but it was in vain. He was dead.
You took the <clr>machine gun<clrEnd> away from him. Now you needed it more than he did.
jump.70.desc:
The lifeless faeyan wasn't too heavy, but the <clr>sniper rifle<clrEnd> on his back made it quite difficult to carry him. You took it off him, and put it on your back quickly. Then you dragged the driver away to a safe distance. Your timing couldn't have been better! A short time later an explosion tore the armored car to pieces.
You examined the faeyan - he was dead.
jump.71.text: Take the box with the military marking on the lid
jump.72.text: Get out all by yourself as quickly as possible
jump.72.desc: That was pretty easy. You kicked the door out, ran from the armored car, which was in flames, and dove to the ground. An instant later a huge blast ripped the vehicle to pieces. The fire blazed upward, incinerating the original plan for the operation. Now you are all alone to face the hostile mercenaries who are scattered along the way to the peleng base.
